questions.knowledgeNote: Two matrices are inverses iff their product (both ways for square matrices) is I.
questions.question: Q6. Prove that [[-3,-2],[5,3]] and [[3,2],[-5,-3]] are inverses of each other.
questions.solution: Product: [[-9+10,-6+6],[15-15,10-9]] = [[1,0],[0,1]] = I. So each is the inverse of the other.

questions.knowledgeNote: det = 1 here, so the inverse equals the adjoint: AA^{-1} = I checks 9 entries.
questions.question: Q9. If A = [[1,2,-2],[-1,3,0],[0,-2,1]], find A^{-1} and verify that AA^{-1} = I.
questions.solution: det A = 1(3-0)-2(-1-0)-2(2-0) = 3+2-4 = 1. Cofactors give adj A = [[3,2,6],[1,1,2],[2,2,5]]. Since det = 1, A^{-1} = adj A (matches the printed key, p281). AA^{-1} = I verified entry by entry.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.9 Ex 9.3 Q9; book p281 = PDF p308 (vision read)
